sources.ref_file_title: CCG+94 - The random oracle hypothesis is false
sources.authors: Richard Chang, Benny Chor, Oded Goldreich, Juris Hartmanis, Johan Håstad, Desh Ranjan, Pankaj Rohatgi
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 49(1):24-39
sources.note: Already in content/References/. Title, authors, venue and the four results used here (for almost all oracles A, IP^A != PSPACE^A and coNP^A not contained in IP^A; extension to multi-prover systems; IPP^A = PSPACE^A for every A) confirmed from the abstract via search snippets; ScienceDirect, ACM DL and Semantic Scholar are blocked by the egress proxy. Not in the vendored cryptobib (journal paper) — keep the inline bibtex on the reference page.

pages.class_justification: CCG+94 refute the Random Oracle Hypothesis unconditionally, so what fails is the implication ROM ⇒ ROH itself, not one proof technique: the class ruled out is `free`. The migrated `relativizing` has no basis in the source and is subsumed anyway — a barrier against `free` kills every class in schema/reduction-classes.yaml.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field. The counterexample is a statement about random oracle worlds; the statement quantifies over the oracle explicitly.
pages.statement: For almost all oracles $A$, $\classIP^A \neq \classPSPACE^A$; in fact $\classcoNP^A \not\subseteq \classIP^A$ — [[CCG+94 - The random oracle hypothesis is false|CCG+94]]. Since [[interactive-proof-systems|IP]] $=$ [[polynomial-space|PSPACE]] holds unrelativized, the [[random-oracle-hypothesis|Random Oracle Hypothesis]] (class relationships holding for almost all oracles hold unrelativized) is false. The results extend to multi-prover proof systems, while the variant class $\mathrm{IPP}$ satisfies $\mathrm{IPP}^A = \classPSPACE^A$ for every oracle $A$ — [[CCG+94 - The random oracle hypothesis is false|CCG+94]].
notes_to_keep: The hyperedge is a meta-statement, not a relation between cryptographic objects: [[random-oracle-model|ROM]] is a computational model and the [[random-oracle-hypothesis|ROH]] a conjecture about relativization. The `class` axis of schema/reduction-classes.yaml does not apply to either endpoint.
flags: no-rom-to-roh-ccg-94: class changed `relativizing` -> `free`. The refutation is unconditional, so it rules out the implication itself; `free`-exclusion subsumes `relativizing`-exclusion under the partial order. If a maintainer prefers to leave the class axis unused for meta-conjectures, `unstated` is the only other defensible value — `relativizing` is not.

no-rom-to-roh-ccg-94: the hyperedge is mistyped. Neither ROM (a model) nor ROH (a meta-conjecture) is a primitive/assumption node, so `hypotheses: [rom]` / `conclusion: random-oracle-hypothesis` is not a construction claim. Consider demoting this to a Known Results bullet on content/Glossary/random-oracle-hypothesis.md.
no-rom-to-roh-ccg-94: the evaluative clause 'among the most compelling counterexamples' and the duplicated intro sentence are dropped by the proposed statement (CLAUDE.md anti-patterns).

pages.wrong_reason: The page asserts an unconditional impossibility nobody has proved. Its source sentence records the absence of a known reduction — 'the search-to-decision reduction for standard LPN does not immediately transfer to the expanding-matrix setting' — which is an open question, not a barrier: no separation, oracle world or meta-reduction is claimed by GHJS25 or anyone else, and GHJS25 Theorem 8.8 merely uses the search variant as an alternative hypothesis for PKE. Known results point the other way: search-to-decision reductions for sparse kLIN over $\FF_2$ exist, with a sample blow-up and a shift in sparsity (Bogdanov–Rosen–Tan, CRYPTO 2025), so a proof that none exists in the expanding-matrix setting would be surprising. With `strength: unconditional` and `consequences: [{kind: contradiction}]` the page states a theorem that does not exist. The orientation is correct (search hard ⇒ decision hard), so the fix is deletion, not inversion; the content belongs on content/Assumptions/noisy-k-lin-over-expanders.md § Search noisy $k$-LIN, phrased as 'no search-to-decision reduction is known for expanding matrices over $\FF_p$'.
flags: no-search-noisy-k-lin-to-noisy-k-lin: DELETE recommended. An open question has been typed as an unconditional barrier; keeping it puts a false theorem in relations.json and in the generated 'Participates in / Barriers' block on content/Assumptions/noisy-k-lin-over-expanders.md.
no-search-noisy-k-lin-to-noisy-k-lin: if the page is kept, `strength: unconditional` must at minimum become a conjectural/open marker and the `consequences.kind: contradiction` entry must be removed.

no-search-noisy-k-lin-to-noisy-k-lin: search-to-decision for sparse kLIN — Andrej Bogdanov, Alon Rosen, Kel Zin Tan, 'Sample Efficient Search to Decision for kLIN', CRYPTO 2025, pp. 203-220, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-01855-7_7 (cryptobib C:BogRosTan25; eprint 2025/1469; suggested key BRT25, no collision in existing-refs.txt). Bibliographic data from the vendored cryptobib; the content ('given a distinguisher for (k-1)LIN with m samples, solve search kLIN with roughly O(nm) samples', mod 2) only from search snippets since eprint and Springer are blocked. Whether it transfers to $\FF_p$ expanding matrices is exactly what the assumption page should state as open. Not proposed as a source: a wrong_claim page takes none.

pages.class_justification: The impossibility is information-theoretic and unconditional: no scheme has both properties, by any construction and under any assumption, so the class ruled out is `free`. The hyperedge's `conclusion: com` is vacuous; the content is the joint unsatisfiability of the two hypotheses (see flags).
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field; the argument is unconditional and holds for interactive commitments too.
pages.statement: No [[commitment-scheme|commitment scheme]] with at least two messages is both [[commitment-scheme#hiding|statistically hiding]] and [[commitment-scheme#binding|statistically binding]] — folklore. The argument is information-theoretic and applies to interactive commitments as well.
pages.sketch: Statistical hiding makes the distributions of the commitment $c$ under $\Com(\pp, m_0; r)$ and $\Com(\pp, m_1; r)$ statistically close for $m_0 \neq m_1$, so all but a negligible fraction of commitments to $m_0$ are also commitments to $m_1$ under some randomness $r'$; an unbounded committer finds $r'$ by exhaustive search and opens the same $c$ to both messages, breaking statistical binding.
flags: no-binding-and-hiding-to-com: the hyperedge is typed with `conclusion: com`, but the theorem is that the two hypotheses are jointly unsatisfiable; the real content sits in `consequences: [{kind: contradiction, target: ""}]` and the `conclusion` field is vacuous. Same shape as any 'these two properties cannot coexist' record — worth a schema note.

no-binding-and-hiding-to-com: genuinely folklore — no attributable origin found; Haitner–Nguyen–Ong–Reingold–Vadhan's statistically-hiding-commitments paper states 'it is easy to see that commitment schemes that are both statistically hiding and statistically binding do not exist' with no citation (search snippet of the Harvard-hosted preprint). If a citable form is preferred over '— folklore', Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography Vol. 1* (2001) §4.8 is the textbook treatment; not proposed as a source because the section could not be checked (publisher hosts blocked).

no-binding-and-hiding-to-com: the four-regime enumeration on content/Primitives/commitment-scheme.md belongs on the primitive page, but regime (4) 'perfectly binding / perfectly hiding — which is impossible' restates the sentence above it and should be dropped (editor lane).

no-binding-and-hiding-to-com: OUTSIDE THIS BATCH, skeptical-checker lane — content/Primitives/commitment-scheme.md § Hiding hands $(c, d) \gets \Com(\pp, m_b; r)$ to the adversary; with $d$ it computes $\Open(\pp, c, d) = m_b$ and wins, so the hiding game as written is unsatisfiable. It should send $c$ only.

sketch: tightened; refers to the commitment $c$ only, since the page's $\Com$ outputs $(c, d)$

sources.authors: Henry Corrigan-Gibbs, Alexandra Henzinger, David J. Wu
sources.note: Already in content/References/; the page slug carries the -chw26 suffix, so this paper is the original by construction. Title, authors, eprint 2026/384 (posted 2026-02-24) and the EUROCRYPT 2026 venue (Springer chapter DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-25330-9_4) confirmed via search snippets; eprint.iacr.org and link.springer.com are blocked by the egress proxy and the paper is not yet in the vendored cryptobib. The abstract's wording 'must run in time Ω(min(√q, 1/δ))' (the paper writes q for the group order) is confirmed by the snippet.

pages.class_justification: A lower bound inside an idealized model rules out every algorithm in that model with no restriction on technique, so it is `free` scoped by the model — the convention the sibling page content/Barriers/no-ggm-to-dlog-sho97.md uses and the one schema/reduction-classes.yaml's `rejected: generic-group` message prescribes.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field, so the model is named in the statement. It is the structured generic-group model of CHW26 — Shoup's GGM extended so that the adversary may exploit the group's structure on at most a $\delta$ fraction of elements and is generic on the rest — which is none of the enumerated `model:` values (it would be `other`).
pages.statement: In the structured generic-group model — [[generic-group-model|Shoup's GGM]] extended so that the adversary may exploit the group's special structure on at most a $\delta$ fraction of group elements and is generic on the rest — every algorithm for [[discrete-logarithm|DLOG]] in a group of prime order $p$ runs in time $\Omega\!\left(\min\!\left(\sqrt{p},\, 1/\delta\right)\right)$ — [[CHW26 - The Structured Generic-Group Model|CHW26]]. This gives tight subexponential lower bounds against index-calculus-style algorithms that exploit the multiplicative structure of smooth integers but are otherwise generic — [[CHW26 - The Structured Generic-Group Model|CHW26]].
notes_to_keep: The structured GGM has no node of its own; it is the `#the-structured-ggm` section of [[generic-group-model]], recorded here as a hypothesis by slug alias.

The bound is stated as a running-time lower bound, while the [[Sho97 - Lower Bounds for Discrete Logarithms and Related Problems|Sho97]] bound on the same source page is a query lower bound; the two are not the same unit and the source page switches between them without comment.

pages.wrong_reason: The source sentence says the enhanced property 'is necessary for constructing OT from TDPs': the EGL construction breaks without it (the receiver must sample an image without learning its preimage), which is not a theorem that no construction of [[oblivious-transfer|OT]] from a plain [[trapdoor-permutation|TDP]] exists. No such separation is known; Hajiabadi (TCC 2018) still frames whether standard TDPs suffice for the OT and NIZK constructions as the motivating open question. As typed, with `strength: unconditional` and `consequences: [{kind: contradiction}]`, the page asserts an unproved impossibility, and it contradicts content/Reductions/tdp-to-ot.md (`kind: equivalence`, TDP ⇔ OT), so the graph carries an edge and its negation. The attributable nearby results are (a) Goldreich–Rothblum, 'Enhancements of Trapdoor Permutations' (GR13, in the wiki), which works out the enhanced and doubly-enhanced notions and why the standard OT and NIZK constructions need them, and (b) Hajiabadi, 'Enhancements Are Blackbox Non-Trivial: Impossibility of Enhanced Trapdoor Permutations from Standard Trapdoor Permutations', TCC 2018, which proves there is no fully-black-box construction of an enhanced TDP from a standard TDP. (b) is the barrier to record, on different endpoints: hypotheses [tdp], conclusion enhanced-trapdoor-permutation, class fully-black-box — not hypotheses [tdp], conclusion ot.
flags: no-tdp-to-ot: HIGH PRIORITY GRAPH INCONSISTENCY — content/Reductions/tdp-to-ot.md asserts TDP ⇔ OT (kind: equivalence) while this barrier asserts no TDP ⇒ OT. Both are unsourced migrations and both carry SUSPECTED notes; the lint's contradiction rule does not fire only because both classes are `unstated`. Resolve them together (the converse OT ⇒ TDP is not known either).

sources.ref_file_title: Bar01 - How to Go Beyond the Black-Box Simulation Barrier
sources.note: Bibliographic data verified against the vendored cryptobib FOCS:Barak01 (FOCS 2001, pp. 106-115, DOI 10.1109/SFCS.2001.959885); use `cryptobib_key: FOCS:Barak01`. Abstract (search snippet): assuming collision-resistant hash functions, a zero-knowledge argument for NP that is constant-round with negligible soundness error, public-coin (Arthur–Merlin) and has a strict-polynomial-time non-black-box simulator. Not an improvement of the barrier but its circumvention — the wiki has no 'circumvents' edge type and `role: improvement` is the only slot that creates the reference page. No key collision in existing-refs.txt.

pages.class_justification: GK96 rule out black-box simulation — simulators that use the cheating verifier only as an oracle — and Barak crosses exactly that line. This is not an RTV04 reduction class: RTV04's classes quantify over a construction and a security reduction between primitives, and zero-knowledge (∃ simulator ∀ verifiers) is not a break-relation of that form, so no value in schema/reduction-classes.yaml is literally established. The migrated `fully-black-box` was an analogy; the honest value is `unstated`, with 'black-box simulation' said in prose.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field. Both results are in the standard model; Bar01 assumes collision-resistant hash functions.
pages.statement: No language outside [[bounded-error-probabilistic-polynomial-time|BPP]] has a constant-round public-coin [[zero-knowledge-proof|zero-knowledge]] proof or [[zero-knowledge-proof#argument-systems|argument]] with negligible soundness error whose simulator uses the cheating verifier only as an oracle, and none has a three-round one, public-coin or not — [[GK96 - On the Composition of Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems|GK96]]. The barrier binds only on black-box simulation: assuming collision-resistant hash functions, a simulator that takes the cheating verifier's code as input gives a constant-round public-coin zero-knowledge argument for [[nondeterministic-polynomial-time|NP]] with negligible soundness error — [[Bar01 - How to Go Beyond the Black-Box Simulation Barrier|Bar01]].
pages.sketch: GK96 run the black-box simulator against a verifier whose messages are a random function of the transcript so far, so rewinding only draws fresh challenges; accepting iff the simulator's output is accepting then decides $L$ in $\classBPP$, since on $x \in L$ the output is accepting by completeness and zero-knowledge, and on $x \notin L$ the simulator's queries define an efficient cheating prover, which soundness defeats. Barak's prover commits to a program and gives a witness-indistinguishable universal argument that $x \in L$ or the committed program predicts the verifier's next message; the simulator commits to the verifier's own code and uses that branch as its witness, with no rewinding.
notes_to_keep: The same barrier is stated at content/Complexity/computational-zero-knowledge.md § Limits of zero-knowledge with no cross-link in either direction.
flags: no-zkp-to-argument-systems: HIGH PRIORITY MODELLING — the migrated text records a barrier CIRCUMVENTION (Barak bypassing GK96), not a barrier. A `circumvents` consequence kind, or a `circumvented-by` frontmatter field, is the structural fix.
